title: eval-harness: add CI hooks for prompt-set regression gating and metrics upload
author: Maya Chen
description: Motivation: prevent prompt-set regressions from landing by adding lightweight CI hooks that run a curated prompt regression suite on diffs and upload evaluation metrics to the central eval service for dashboarding. Design: add a GH Actions workflow (eval-harness/.github/workflows/prompt-regression.yml) that triggers on PRs for eval-harness and selected runtime changes, a thin runner (eval-harness/ci/hooks/prompt_regression_runner.py) that runs only affected prompt-sets based on changed examples, and a secure uploader (eval-harness/eval/metrics/uploader.py) that sends time-series metrics and per-prompt artifacts to the eval metrics ingestion API. Checklist: [x] Add GH Actions workflow with required permissions and secrets [x] Implement runner with diff-aware selection and caching [x] Add metrics uploader with retry/backoff and payload size safeguards [x] Wire up tests + integration job that runs in staging [x] Update docs with operational runbook and failure modes. Testing summary: unit tests for runner + uploader, integration run in staging showing end-to-end upload and dashboard ingestion, and benchmarked run-time cost (<30s median for small PRs). Rollout: feature gated by repo label (eval-run) and opt-out via .evalignore; start as optional for a week, then flip to required. Related: ENG-1289 (eval gating), ENG-1402 (metrics pipeline integration), SUP-4421 (customer incident prompting faster detection).
